description: Foreign-runtime failure scenarios that every wrapper runs against the actual engine before it qualifies. Each call names a C function, its arguments in prose, and the exact status it returns.

scenarios.description: Zero, an identifier that was never issued, and an identifier from the other family are unknown.

calls.arguments: a live engine, document zero, and writable output
a live engine and the largest 64-bit document identifier
a live engine, document zero, a one-byte URL, and writable output
a live engine and a response for request zero
a live engine, the largest 64-bit request identifier, and the unsupported_version reason
a live engine and a live document's identifier used as a request
a live engine, a live request's identifier used as a document, and writable output

effects: No output byte changes.
The engine queues no event and no input.
The live document stays loading, and its request still accepts a response.

scenarios.description: A document or request identifier from one engine is unknown in another engine.

engine B and a request of engine A
engine B and a request of engine A
engine A and a response for its own request

effects: Neither engine changes, and no output byte changes.
Engine A's document stays loading, and its request still accepts a response.

scenarios.description: A destroyed document, a request that a step ended, and a request that a reload ended are unknown.

the request that the reload cancelled
a budget that applies a queued response
the request whose response the step applied

effects: Identifiers are never reused, so a retired identifier stays unknown.
No output byte changes.

scenarios.description: Every owner-thread function called from a thread that did not create the engine is refused before any other argument check.

calls.arguments: the engine from another thread
the engine and a live document from another thread
the engine and a live document from another thread
the engine and a live document from another thread
the engine and a response for a live request from another thread
the engine and a live request from another thread
the engine and a live request from another thread
the engine from another thread
the engine from another thread
the engine from another thread
the engine and a null output from another thread
the engine and document zero from another thread
the engine, a live document, and a null output, then an output size one byte short, from another thread
the engine, a live document, and a null URL with a nonzero length, then a null output, from another thread
the engine and a null response, then a response whose struct_size is one byte short, from another thread
the engine, a live request, and the unknown reason zero from another thread
the engine and request zero from another thread
the engine and a null output, then an output size one byte short, from another thread
the engine and a null output, then a zero output size, from another thread
writable output from another thread

effects: No engine, document, request, queued input, or event changes.
No output byte changes.
A call with an invalid argument also returns wrong_thread, so the thread check precedes every other argument check.
fp_engine_destroy takes no argument other than the engine, so only its call with a valid engine applies.
fp_query_capabilities follows the any-thread rule and succeeds, and fp_abi_revision returns the revision from any thread.

scenarios.description: A host cancellation of a request without a queued answer queues input, and a step fails the document.

calls.arguments: a live request without a queued answer
a budget of eight
the same request again

effects: The document stays loading until the step applies the cancellation.
The step applies one input and fails the document.
The step announces request_cancelled and then document_state_changed to failed with no rejection reason.

scenarios.description: A queued answer blocks a host cancellation, and an engine cancellation by reload discards the queued answer.

calls.arguments: a response for a live request
the answered request
the answered request
a second response for the answered request
the same document, which cancels the answered request
a budget of eight
a response for the cancelled request

effects: The reload announces request_cancelled for the first request and request_issued for the second request.
The step applies nothing, and the document stays loading.
A response for the second request later loads the document with exactly that body.

scenarios.description: Destroying a document with an outstanding request, a queued answer, and undrained events cancels the request and keeps other documents.

calls.arguments: a response for the doomed document's request
the doomed document
repeated until the kind is none
a budget of eight
a response for the other document's request

effects: The undrained issuance event of the ended request has a null URL and a zero length.
The destruction announces request_cancelled after the earlier events.
The step applies nothing because the queued answer was discarded.
The destroyed document and its request are unknown, and the other document stays loading.

scenarios.description: Destroying an engine with outstanding requests, queued answers, loaded bodies, and undrained events releases everything.

calls.arguments: a zero budget, which reports queued input and ready events
the engine

effects: The destruction succeeds without draining events or applying input.
A runtime with an allocation tracker observes no leaked engine storage.

scenarios.description: Each operation that allocates returns out_of_memory at each of its allocations and changes nothing.
scenarios.reason: The C ABI takes no allocator, so a C caller cannot induce an allocation failure inside the engine.

calls.arguments: options with an allocator whose next allocation fails
an engine whose next allocation fails
an engine whose first, then second, then later allocation fails
an engine whose input queue must grow
an engine whose full input queue must grow
an engine whose full input queue must grow
an engine whose event queue must grow to announce an applied host cancellation
a loading document in an engine whose every later allocation fails

effects: No engine handle, identifier, or output byte is written.
The documents, requests, queued inputs, and events stay unchanged.
The same call succeeds once allocation succeeds, and destroying the engine frees every allocated byte.
fp_document_destroy allocates nothing, so it succeeds and announces the cancellation while every allocation fails.

scenarios.description: A response body beyond max_response_body_bytes returns limit_exceeded, and a body at the bound succeeds.

calls.arguments: a body bound of sixteen bytes
a seventeen-byte body
a sixteen-byte body

effects: The oversized response queues nothing, and the request stays live.
The document loads with exactly the sixteen-byte body.

scenarios.description: A load beyond max_outstanding_requests returns limit_exceeded, and a reload of a loading document stays within the bound.

calls.arguments: a bound of two outstanding requests
a third document while two requests are outstanding
a document that is already loading
a budget that applies one response
the third document

effects: The refused load writes no output, queues no event, and leaves the third document empty.
The third document loads after a request ends.

scenarios.description: A foreign exception or panic in host code never unwinds across the C ABI, and the engine stays usable afterward.
scenarios.reason: C has no exceptions or unwinding, and the engine never calls host code, so a C caller has no failure to propagate.

calls.arguments: the engine, after which host code fails
a response for the live request after the host failure
a budget of eight
the engine

effects: Every C function returns a plain status, so no exception, panic, or error union crosses the boundary.
A wrapper catches a host exception or panic before it reaches a C frame.
The engine keeps its state through the host failure, loads the document, and frees every allocated byte on destruction.
